body:
Double garage doors in Milton Keynes for wider openings

Double garage doors in Milton Keynes cover a surprising range of jobs. Some customers have a classic two-car garage with one wide opening; others have a pair of single openings side by side and want two matching doors; and a growing number want to knock two singles into one so it's easier to park a modern SUV. Whatever your layout, the key challenge with a double door is the same: a wide door is heavy, so it has to be properly specified, balanced and fitted to run safely for years.

We supply and fit every main type of double garage door, manual or electric, and we'll help you choose based on how you use the space, how much headroom you have and what suits the front of your house.

How wide are double garage doors?

In the UK, standard double garage doors are commonly made in widths from around 14 feet (about 4.27 metres) up to 16 feet (about 4.88 metres), with 7 feet (2.13 metres) a typical height. Many modern homes have openings that don't match these "standard" sizes, and made-to-measure doors are widely available. For a full breakdown of single and double sizes, read our garage door sizes guide.

How wide can a roller garage door be? Most domestic aluminium roller doors go up to roughly 5 to 6 metres wide, depending on the slat profile and wind loading. Sectional doors can go wider still. We'll confirm limits for your opening at the survey.

Types of double garage door

Double sectional garage doors

Our most popular choice for wide openings. Insulated steel panels lift vertically and run back under the ceiling, so you can park right up to the door on the drive. A double sectional is quiet, well sealed and ideal for automation. See sectional garage doors for panel styles and finishes.

Double roller garage doors

Roller doors coil into a box above the opening, saving all your ceiling space. Wider roller doors use stronger slats and a heavier-duty motor, and they're nearly always electric. Find out more on our roller garage doors page.

Double up and over garage doors

The budget-friendly option. Steel up and over doors in double widths are widely available in canopy or retractable gear, and they can often be automated later. They do swing out a little as they open, so you need clear space in front.

Wooden and side hinged double garage doors

Timber double garage doors, often as two or three pairs of side hinged leaves, have real kerb appeal on period and rural properties around Olney and the villages. Oak, hardwood and engineered timber are all options. They need regular treatment, but nothing quite matches the look. Our wooden garage doors page goes into the detail.

Pros and cons of one wide door vs two single doors

  • One wide door: easier parking, no central pier to clip, one motor and one remote. But if it breaks, both bays are affected, and the door is heavier.
  • Two single doors: independent operation, lighter doors, and if one fails you can still use the other bay. The central pier does narrow each opening.

Insulated double garage doors are well worth considering if the garage is attached to the house or used as a gym or workshop — a large uninsulated door loses a lot of heat. Our insulated garage doors page explains the options.

Converting two single garage doors to a double

Turning two single openings into one wide opening is a structural job. The central brick pier is holding up part of the wall above, so it has to be replaced by a new, correctly sized steel or concrete lintel. That usually means a structural engineer's calculation, building control notification and a builder to carry out the brickwork before the new door goes in.

As a rough guide, the building work alone often costs several thousand pounds before the new door is added, depending on the wall above, the finish and access. We can fit the door once the opening is ready and can talk to your builder about the exact sizes needed. Going the other way — converting double garage doors to a single, perhaps for a garage conversion — is also a building job, typically involving new brickwork, a window or a smaller door.

Who suits a double garage door?

  • Two-car households who want to park both vehicles under cover.
  • Homes with a single wide opening where the old door is worn out.
  • Anyone who uses half the garage for storage, a workshop or bikes and wants easy access.
  • Owners of larger family homes in areas like Shenley Brook End, Walnut Tree and Monkston, where double garages are common.

Below are indicative UK guide ranges for supplying and fitting a double door in 2026. Exact prices depend on width, insulation, finish, motor and the condition of the opening, and are confirmed in writing after a free survey.

Wooden side hinged double doors£3,000–£6,500Species, glazing and finish affect price

Electric double garage doors fitted prices vary most on motor quality and door size. For more on running costs and add-ons, see how much electric garage doors cost.

How we fit a double garage door

A double door is usually a two-person job. We measure the opening, headroom and side room, check the lintel and floor level, and look at where power can be supplied. On the day we remove the old door, install frames, tracks or guides, hang the door, and balance springs or set the motor's force and travel limits. Safety edges and photocells are tested before we hand over. Most double doors are fitted in a single day.

Tip: measure your car's width with the mirrors out and compare it with the clear opening, not the brick-to-brick width. Frames and guides take up a little space on each side.

faqs.q: How much do double garage doors cost?
faqs.a: As a guide, a manual steel double up and over door fitted typically starts around £1,300, while electric double roller and sectional doors usually range from about £2,200 to £5,000 fitted. Wooden double doors can cost more. Your exact price depends on size, finish and motor, and we confirm it in writing after a free survey.

faqs.q: Can I convert two single garage doors to a double?
faqs.a: Usually, yes, but it involves removing the central pier and fitting a properly sized lintel, which needs a structural calculation and building control involvement. A builder does the structural work, then we fit the new wide door. We're happy to advise on the door size your builder should aim for so everything fits neatly.

They can be. Roller and sectional double doors are nearly always supplied electric, and many double up and over doors can be fitted with a motor. Because wide doors are heavy, automation makes daily use much easier, and modern motors include safety features that stop and reverse the door if it meets an obstruction.

faqs.q: What size is a standard double garage door in the UK?
faqs.a: Common standard double sizes run from roughly 14 to 16 feet wide (about 4.27 to 4.88 metres) and around 7 feet (2.13 metres) high. Many homes have non-standard openings, so we always measure carefully, and made-to-measure doors are available. See our UK garage door sizes guide for more detail.

faqs.q: Is one double door or two single doors better?
faqs.a: It depends on how you use the garage. One wide door makes parking easier and needs just one motor, while two singles let you open each bay separately and mean one breakdown won't block both spaces. Where a central pier already exists, two singles avoid structural work. We'll help you weigh it up at the survey.
